text: Fine-tuning language models under GPU memory limits requires balancing static weights, optimizer states, gradient graphs, and activation footprints.
This note evaluates low-rank factorizations, singular value decomposition schedulers, weight decomposition, quantization-aware tuning, and bias tuning.
We separate design choices from measured benchmarks, formulate a controlled experiment isolating activation overhead from adapter rank scaling, and evaluate an unverified laboratory memory claim.

section: Limitations, Boundary Conditions, and Unverified Claims
text: Hardware and methodological constraints govern low-memory adaptation.

section: Limitations, Boundary Conditions, and Unverified Claims
text: Memory reductions cannot be transferred across different GPU architectures; memory bus bandwidth and kernel implementations vary across Ampere, Ada Lovelace, and Hopper architectures.

section: Limitations, Boundary Conditions, and Unverified Claims
text: Dequantization and paged memory transfers also incur runtime overheads that degrade training throughput.

section: Limitations, Boundary Conditions, and Unverified Claims
text: We explicitly address an unverified claim circulating in laboratory planning: Someone in our lab says, 'Our pilot halves training memory compared with LoRA.' This statement is entirely undocumented: it specifies no model architecture, precision baseline, batch size, sequence length, or profiling tool.

section: Limitations, Boundary Conditions, and Unverified Claims
text: As established by, static base weights and activation buffers account for the vast majority of memory in standard LoRA; halving training memory cannot occur via adapter adjustments without altering base weight precision or activation caching.

text: Because no empirical report, hardware telemetry, or code artifacts have been supplied, this assertion remains explicitly unverified and must not serve as an experimental premise or baseline.
